title: Implement YAML config file loader
objective: Provide a config loader so the service can read its listen address and log level from a YAML file at startup, with sensible defaults when the file is absent.
current_state: internal/config/ package does not exist yet. cmd/server/main.go already calls config.Load(configPath) in anticipation of this package, so the binary will not build until this task lands.
target_behavior: internal/config exports Load(path string) (*Config, error), where Config has fields ListenAddr and LogLevel (both string). Load reads YAML from path; a missing file yields default values (ListenAddr=":8080", LogLevel="info") with a nil error; a present file's fields override the defaults for any field it sets; malformed YAML returns a non-nil, descriptive error and a nil *Config.
interfaces_to_preserve: func Load(path string) (*Config, error) signature, exactly as already called from cmd/server/main.go
input_format: path: string, filesystem path to a YAML file; the file may not exist.
output_format: *Config{ListenAddr string, LogLevel string}, error. error is non-nil only when the file exists and its contents are malformed YAML.
error_handling: A missing config file must return default Config values with a nil error, not an error.
Malformed YAML must return a wrapped error naming the file path and the underlying parse failure, with a nil *Config.
completion_criteria: Load() on a nonexistent path returns &Config{ListenAddr: ":8080", LogLevel: "info"} with a nil error.
Load() on internal/config/testdata/sample-config.yaml returns the ListenAddr and LogLevel values specified in that file.
Load() on a malformed YAML fixture returns a non-nil error and a nil *Config.
go test ./internal/config/... passes with zero failures.
manual_verification: Once both T-401 and T-402 have landed and the binary builds, run the server with and without a config file present and confirm the listen address matches expectations in each case.

delegation.justification: T-402 is one of two independently verifiable work groups; its files, interfaces, data, generated output, shared state, and user flow are disjoint from T-401, the batch has no cross-group dependency edge, and planned_workers is bounded by observed native capacity.
